inventory.visualPurpose: The Kaplan-Meier stepped-curve figure (book 259, bottom): a two-arm time-to-event plot — survival probability (y-axis, ticks 1.0–0.2) vs length of time (x-axis, letters X/Y/Z at the two event times and the end of follow-up) — with the Drug and Control curves stepping down at events X and Y and ending flat at Z; the page's graphic representation of 'time-to-event' data and the visual anchor the hazard-ratio block's relative-slopes derivation points back to
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE VECTOR LINE ART, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images on the page; geometry pinned by PyMuPDF vector paths + the VLM pass at 120dpi, staging-pubh7/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): a tan/brown L-shaped axis — vertical y-axis with NINE tick marks labeled 1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2 top to bottom (no 0.1/0.0) and a rotated y-axis label 'Survival probability' (reading bottom-to-top), horizontal x-axis with FOUR unlabeled tick marks and the label 'Time' printed below-right of center; below the axis the letters X, Y, Z mark the last three ticks (X and Y = the two event/drop times, Z = the end of follow-up). TWO stepped curves: 'Drug' (label blue #729ac4, printed just above the curve's final flat segment; curve strokes blue with a GREEN initial segment and green start dot) and 'Control' (label yellow #fcc00d, same placement; curve yellow/gold). Both curves start at 1.0 sharing the opening flat segment; at X the Drug curve steps down ONE tick to 0.9 (green landing dot) while Control steps down THREE ticks to 0.7 (yellow landing dot) — the shared vertical drop at X is drawn TWO-TONE (green above 0.9, yellow below to 0.7); at Y Drug steps a HALF-TICK to ≈0.85 (blue dot) and Control TWO ticks to ≈0.5 (yellow dot); both then run flat to the end of follow-up at Z with endpoint dots and no further drop (Drug ends ≈0.85, Control ≈0.5). Small gray Rx logo at the figure's lower right. The raw text layer interleaves the labels (indd slug after the heading; the nine y-axis numbers AFTER the two likelihood-ratio rule sentences of raw lines 140-141, which print ABOVE the KM heading and belong to the likelihood-ratios topic; then Drug / Control / X / Y / Time / Z) — documented, never quoted across the boundary.
